processing: Solomon's seal root is roasted and steeped or simmered; it is also sold as a liquid extract to dilute.
harvest_season: Sold as a dried, roasted root all year; little is documented about harvest timing.
appearance_dry: Typically golden-brown roasted root pieces; also sold as a dark liquid extract.
appearance_liquor: Typically a clear light amber, as with other roasted Korean grain and root teas.
taste_profile: Smooth and mildly nutty, with a roasted aroma.

brewing.notes: A home starting point for loose root, not a fixed recipe. Extracts are diluted with hot or cold water to the strength you like, so follow the packet.

vintage_note: No vintages. It is sold as a packaged roasted product, so go by the packing date, as with other roasted herbal teas.
description:
Dunggulle-cha is a Korean infusion of Solomon's seal root, usually roasted. There is no tea plant in it, so as with other root infusions it has no caffeine.

Roasting sets the character of the cup, which is smooth and mildly nutty with a roasted aroma.

It can be drunk hot or cold. Extracts make this easy: add more or less water until the strength suits you.

Read the ingredients when buying, since products under this name can differ in how much root they contain.
history: Little is documented in detail about the history of dunggulle-cha as a drink. Today it is sold as a packaged Korean tea, including as a roasted root extract.
